title: Decide what Cancel does on an established-but-stalled SMB session (about 60 s wait)
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C2 A person's decision between (a) abandoning the scan thread and (b) keeping the wait and saying so in the Stopping state: missing
C3 A design pass for the chosen option, before any build: missing
C4 Option (a) implemented: the scan thread is abandoned so Cancel frees the app before the client timeout: missing
C5 Option (b) implemented: the Stopping state says a wait of about 60 s is possible: partial

C2: does the person accept option (b), keep the wait and show it (which retires C4), or choose (a), abandoning the scan thread? (a) replaces this design and needs spike 2 run first for a retention bound, a late-write fence in the Scan Engine at counting-rule risk tier, and a rule for holding an abandoned store and a new scan against the 1 GB budget. A softer variant (return to a cancelled state at once and block a new scan until the old one releases) carries the same fence and retention costs.

Will the person run the timed real disconnects (Wi-Fi off, `tailscale down`, sleep about 2 minutes mid-scan, 3 runs each, timing Cancel to scan return against a slow second-host share) before or at validate? Only they can, and the result decides whether 'usually about a minute' is true and whether (b) still stands.

Wording as a pure function in its own file linked into Core.Tests (this design) versus inline branches in MainWindow.xaml.cs proved only through the hook (the proposal). The link keeps the 90 s branch under test without an App test project, at the price of one linked file.
Recording the decision in the existing SL-020-scanner.md section (the proposal, kept) versus a new SL-038 document. Either is findable, but two places can disagree.

A 2 s gate with a 90 s second wording versus one wording with no boundary. One wording would remove a branch, but it would either claim about a minute where that is unmeasured or say nothing useful past it.
StallRig as a linked-source console outside the slnx versus a project inside it or a rig mode in the hook. The chosen form matches how the hook is already built and kept out of the default build.

Whether 'Closing the window quits at once' should be on screen at all, or whether the escape stays unspoken. It is kept because the person has nothing else to do for a minute. It is backed by its own opt-in case.
Naming the hook env vars after spike 4's scratch copy (FSA_HOOK_ARMED, FSA_HOOK_CANCEL_DELAY_MS, FSA_HOOK_CLOSE_DELAY_MS) versus the proposal's FSA_HOOK_CANCEL_AFTER_MARKER.
